title: How a river changes from mountain to sea
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: How does a river change along its course?
Why are rivers fast in the mountains?
What landforms are found in each part of a river?

explain.say: A river begins at its source, often a spring, a lake or melting snow high in the hills. From there it flows downhill all the way to the sea.

draw.text: How a river changes from mountain to sea

explain.say: In the steep upper course, the river is small and fast-flowing. It cuts mostly downward, carving a narrow V-shaped valley with rapids and waterfalls.
In the middle course, the land is gentler and the river is wider. It cuts sideways more than down, swinging into meanders.
In the lower course, the land is nearly flat. The river is wide and deep, floods spread silt across a floodplain, and it drops its load where it meets the sea, sometimes building a delta.

faq.q: How does a river change along its course?
faq.a: Near the source it is narrow, steep and cuts downward into V-shaped valleys. Further on it gets wider and deeper, with gentler slopes and meanders, until it crosses a flat floodplain to the sea.
asks: What are the stages of a river?

faq.q: Why are rivers fast in the mountains?
faq.a: In the mountains they look fast and splashy because the slope is steep and the bed is rocky. Surprisingly, the average flow in the lower course is often just as fast, because the deep, smooth channel has less friction.
asks: Is a river faster near the sea?

faq.q: What landforms are found in each part of a river?
faq.a: The upper course has V-shaped valleys, waterfalls and rapids. The middle course has meanders. The lower course has floodplains, oxbow lakes, levees and deltas or estuaries.

faq.q: What is the source of a river?
faq.a: The source is where a river begins, such as a spring, a marsh, a lake or a melting glacier, usually on high ground.

faq.q: Why is a river V-shaped near its source?
faq.a: The steep river cuts down into its bed quickly, while weathering and landslides wear the valley sides back into sloping walls, making a V-shape.

facts: A river's long profile, from source to mouth, is steep at first and becomes gentler downstream.
The Nile and the Amazon are the two longest rivers in the world, each over 6,400 kilometres long.

quiz.say: Where would you most likely find a waterfall along a river?
quiz.show: Waterfalls are most common in the…
quiz.why: The steep upper course, with bands of hard and soft rock, is where waterfalls and rapids form.

wrong.1: The lower course is gentle and flat, with meanders and floodplains.
wrong.2: A delta is at the flat river mouth, with no big drops.
